entry.idea: Most music apps just let you listen or use AI to generate a whole song for you, so this studio makes small, playful apps that get people directly involved in making sounds and music themselves.
entry.lesson: A well-known figure from a big platform can use their credibility and taste to launch small, experimental products before settling on one core product.
entry.name: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya

growth.reason: This is a brand-new pre-seed company with no prior round or usage numbers to compare against.

market.reason: Consumer music-creation apps are a real market of interested hobbyists and musicians worldwide, but it is a niche next to mainstream music streaming.

tech.reason: The apps are experimental and creative, but public reports do not describe a hard-to-copy technical edge, and sources even disagree on how much AI is involved.

entry.twist: It is run by a former Spotify leader and releases its work as small experimental 'singles' style apps rather than one big product, with reports differing on how much of the music-making is AI-driven versus hands-on.
entry.who_pays: Not yet clear from public reporting; likely everyday consumers who would pay to use or subscribe to its music-making apps.
entry.why_now: People are tired of passively consuming AI-made content and want playful, hands-on ways to create music themselves, especially as making music with software gets easier.
